newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - May 16.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - May 16.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Friday :

* On Thursday, the Dow Jones industrial average set another record by rising 47.39 points to close at 7,333.55 points and bond prices also rose, rebounding after investors shrugged off a rise in consumer prices last month.
* Several people were injured in violence involving supporters of Indonesia's ruling Golkar party during election campaigning in the capital Jakarta on Thursday, witnesses said.

* Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said on Thursday the government will consider offering new incentives to oil investors in an effort to boost exploration but added tax laws could not be relaxed.

* On Thursday, the Jakarta Composite Index was off 13.30 points, or about 1.98 percent, to close at 656.99 points on sporadic election violence and fears of a meltdown in Thailand, economists and traders said.
Brokers said political tensions could prompt further selling in the local market on Friday even though the fall in the index on Thursday was more related to worries in Thailand.
* On Friday, the rupiah soared to 2,421.25/6.00 at 0150 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,433.00/34.00 after rumours that Malaysia was planning to scrap swap facilities.
* Conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers on reports on Thursday that its unit had invested $100 million in the Iridium sate communications system.

* Secondary shoe-maker Telagamas Pertiwi on a report in Bisnis Indonesia newspaper that it will become a holding company of four subsidiaries and that its total assets would reach 220.4 billion rupiah, a rise of about 335.5 percent.
* Medium-size bank Tiara on a report in Bisnis Indonesia newspaper that it had received a $20 million syndicated loan from overseas banks.
* Small-sized Bank Pikko on reports the Capital Market Supervisory Agency had handed down penalties on parties involved in the Bank Pikko share scam.
* Tourism firm Bayu Buana following active trading on Wednesday due to market talk of a possible take-over.
* Indosat and Lonsum after announcements of rises in their first quarter results.
* Sorini and Aneka Kimia on renewed market talk of a possible merger.
